message: The acknowledgement watermark is the goal entity's updatedAt, which any write to the goal bumps - including the staff member's own edits in the NS calculator. After a user views the card, opens the wizard and saves a field, the card returns on the dashboard saying "Your goal changed since you last looked", which is false.

The GqlMockedProvider UserOption mock is not parameterized by the `key` variable, so it returns the same fixture ({key:"user_type_verified", value:"true"}) for both ConfirmUserGroupModal's check and NewStaffGoalReadyCard's own `new_staff_goal_acknowledged_goal-1` lookup. The test only passes because "true" happens to parse as an invalid Date (NaN), so it coincidentally looks unacknowledged rather than because the mock actually answers the right key.
No test covers a GraphQL error response for NewStaffGoalReady or UserOption, so a regression that leaves the card stuck loading/crashing on an Apollo error would go undetected.

The card forks the eligibility gate every other nsGoalCalculator entry point uses: it checks only DISABLE_NS_GOAL_CALCULATOR and inNsGoalCalcIneligibleGroup, omitting reportsDisabled and the userType check. The card and its link can therefore appear for users the nav hides the tool from, and for users the page itself answers with LimitedAccess.

SentGoalCard does `if (loading || ...) return null` on useUserOptionQuery, whose loading flag goes true again on every refetch under the app-wide cache-and-network + notifyOnNetworkStatusChange policy. This is the documented refetch-flash bug: an already-visible, undismissed card will vanish and reappear on refocus/cache invalidation, not just on first load.

acknowledge() has no error handling on updateUserOption, and no test exercises a rejected mutation; because dismissed is set to true unconditionally before the request resolves, a failed save leaves the card permanently hidden for that session with nothing asserting or fixing that behavior.

The acknowledgement timestamp is parsed with `new Date(string)` instead of Luxon, so a partially parseable non-ISO value (e.g. "2026" or "Sep 2026") reads as a valid acknowledgement in the past and silently flips the card to the "Your MPD goal was updated" copy. The repo convention is `DateTime.fromISO(...).isValid`, because `new Date(arbitraryString)` parsing is implementation-defined per spec.

`if (loading) return null` blanks the card on every refetch of the UserOption query, not just the first load, because the client sets `fetchPolicy: cache-and-network` with `notifyOnNetworkStatusChange: true` — so `loading` goes true again on each remount while cached `data` is already present. That reintroduces exactly the card flash the comment two lines above says this code exists to avoid.

`acknowledge()` sets `dismissed` to true and fires `updateUserOption` without awaiting or catching it, so a failed write produces an unhandled promise rejection and leaves the card hidden for the rest of the session while nothing was persisted — it silently returns on the next page load. The optimistic response is never rolled back into visible state.

New key "Your goal changed since you last looked..." is inserted after "Your MPD goal was updated" instead of before "Your MPD goal is ready", which is where crowdin/sort-translations.js (a.localeCompare(b)) would place it.
